labels.name: life_threatening_rescue
labels.definition: Message indicates a person or group is in immediate life-threatening danger and needs physical extraction or rescue right now (trapped, drowning, buried, stranded by rising water/fire).
examples_of_edge_cases: water is up to my chest and rising, kids on the roof with me, hurry
building next door collapsed, i can hear someone screaming under the rubble
stuck in my car on the bridge, engine is off, water coming in fast cant open door

labels.name: medical_emergency
labels.definition: Message describes a person needing urgent medical attention (injury, unconsciousness, labor, chest pain, severe bleeding) but who is not currently trapped or in imminent physical danger of the environment.
examples_of_edge_cases: my dad fell during the quake and hes bleeding a lot from his head, still conscious
neighbor is having contractions, roads are blocked, need an ambulance or paramedic
elderly woman collapsed, breathing but not responding, we are at the shelter entrance

labels.name: hazard_report
labels.definition: Message reports an environmental or infrastructure danger (fire, gas leak, downed power line, collapsing structure, blocked/flooded road) that responders need to address or route around, without a specific person currently trapped or injured.
examples_of_edge_cases: gas smell really strong near 5th and main, nobody hurt yet but its getting worse
power line down across Oak St, sparking, cars driving around it, someone will get hurt
the dam near our town looks like its cracking, no evacuation order yet

labels.name: resource_need
labels.definition: Message requests non-emergency supplies or support such as food, water, shelter, blankets, medication refills, or transportation, where lack of the resource is not immediately life-threatening.
examples_of_edge_cases: we're okay but out of drinking water at the community center, about 40 people
does anyone have extra insulin, my prescription got washed away
need a ride to the shelter, roads near us are fine just no car

labels.name: situational_update
labels.definition: Message shares status, location safety, general observations, offers of help, or coordination info that responders may find useful for awareness but does not itself request or require dispatch.
examples_of_edge_cases: just checked in, we're safe at my sister's place across town
power is back on in the north side as of 10pm
volunteers with boats are gathering at the church parking lot if anyone needs to organize

labels.name: non_actionable
labels.definition: Message is irrelevant, unclear, spam, a joke, or otherwise provides nothing responders can act on or use.
examples_of_edge_cases: lol this weather app is so wrong again
is anyone else's wifi down or is it just me
praying for everyone stay safe out there 🙏🙏

generation_personas: A teenager livetweeting an earthquake from under a desk, using hashtags, emojis, and abbreviated slang, phone at 15% battery
A middle-aged flood victim texting 911's SMS line in all caps with typos, panicking, short fragmented sentences
An elderly man dictating a message to his grandson over the phone, formal and slightly confused phrasing, includes unnecessary pleasantries
A volunteer disaster-response coordinator posting structured, calm updates to a community forum with timestamps and locations
A non-native English speaker (recent immigrant) describing a gas leak using translated sentence structure and simple vocabulary
A person with limited literacy texting phonetically spelled words and no punctuation, describing a collapsed roof
A local news intern relaying verified facts from scanner traffic in terse, factual, third-person style
A bored teenager trolling the emergency hotline with a fake or joking report, casual internet slang
A person trapped in rubble typing one-handed on a cracked phone screen with a dying battery, using very short broken phrases
A rural farmer with spotty cell signal sending a voice-to-text message full of transcription errors about downed power lines and livestock
A nurse at an overwhelmed shelter clinic typing quick clinical shorthand about patient needs
An anxious parent separated from their child during evacuation, sending frantic, repetitive messages with pleading tone
